For Petitioner : Mr.R.Pravesh

For Respondent : Mr.S.P.Karthick  Government Advocate  1/8 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  TR.CMP M.D.Venkadesan vs The Special Tahsildar (L.A) on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105662538/

ORDER This petition has been filed by the revision petitioner to withdraw R.F.C.T.L.A.R.R.OP.No.09 of 2023 from the file of the Principal District Judge at Dharmapuri and transfer the same to the Principal District Court at Chennai.

2. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted submitted that R.F.C.T.L.A.R.R.OP.No.09 of 2023 has been filed by the Special Tahsildar (L.A), SIPCOT UNIT-I,
Dharmapuri against the petitioner herein namely Thiru.M.D. Vengadesan, S/o.Duraisami.
The revision petitioner is aged about 88 years.
He is residing at No.35, Bhagirathi Ammal Street,T.Nagar, Chennai.

3. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that the revision petitioner is the sole and absolute owner of property comprised in Survey No.346 measuring an extent of 1.85 hectares in Thadangam Village, Nallampalli Taluk in and by way of a Deed of Settlement dated 08.12.1986 registered as Document No.1787 of 1986 on the file of the S.R.O.Dharmapuri.
Ever since then, the petitioner was in sole and absolute https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis possession and enjoyment of the property without any interference or disturbance whatsoever.
He has further submitted that the petitioner had mutated revenue records in his individual name and was also issued Patta No.1215 in his name in respect of the aforesaid property in 2014.

Thereafter, a Notification dated 22.12.2016 under Sections 3 and 4 of the Tamil Nadu Acquisition of Land for Industrial Purposes Act, 1997 was issued by the Collector for acquiring the entire property of the petitioner.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu Acquisition of Land for Industrial Purposes Act, 1997
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner further submitted that the land was acquired as per the TNALIP Act, 1997, for formation of new SIPCOT Industrial Park at Thadangam Village in Nallampatti Taluk, Dharmapuri District.
The Special Tahsildar(L.A) SIPCOT UNIT-I, Dharmapuri had acquired the petitioner's land and the same was registered vide Document No.1787 of 1986 on the file of the Sub Registrar Office, Dharmapuri.
Thereby, the petitioner is entitled for award amount.

5. The learned counsel also stated that the Special Tahsildar (LA), SIPCOT Unit-II, Dharmapuri under Section 77(2) of R.F.C.T.L.A.R.R Act and under Section 10(3) of T.N.A.L.I.P, 1997, vide ROC.No.35/2016 Unit- https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis II dated 23.08.2021 has submitted a cheque bearing Cheque.No.528810 dated 23.01.2023 drawn on Indian Bank, Dharmapuri for Rs.57,28,389/- to the revision petitioner/land owner, but, the land owner did not submit the records and refused to acknowledge the receipt of the compensation.

6. Moreover, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner has also submitted that the petition in R.F.C.T.L.A.R.R.OP.No.09 of 2023 has been filed in the year 2023, the petitioner has become very old and he will not be in a position to travel to the said Court.

He submits that the petitioner is the owner of the 1.85 hectares in the above said village which was alienated by way of settlement deed dated 08.12.1986 registered as Document No.1787/1986 and he is in absolute possession and enjoyment of the property which stands in his name also issue Patta.No.1215 in the year 2014 and M.D.Venkadesan vs The Special Tahsildar (L.A) on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105662538/
2
land acquisition proceedings has been initiated.
7. The petitioner has gone through the notification issued by the Collector.
It is seen that the petitioner's mother was said to be the wife of an unknown Raji Gounder while he and her mother were shown as joint owners of the same.

Immediately upon receipt of the notification on 06.01.2017,
he https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis had issued a letter to the Special District Revenue Officer dated 06.01.2017 enclosing a copy of the documents and revenue records in his name and raised objections to the notice issued by the Collector.

Inspite of production of the said documents at the time of enquiry on 10.12.2017, both the fresh notification dated 17.07.2020 which was published in the Gazette as well as the award dated 23.08.2021, contained the same mistakes and falsified information.

Further, the petitioner has not received any notice as contemplated under Section 7(2)
of the Tamil Nadu Acquisition of Land for Industrial Purposes Act, 1997.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Now the petitioner wants to seek transfer of the same and if the said cases were transferred, it will help him and he seeks for transfer of the said original petition pending before the said Principal District Court Dharmapuri to Principal District Judge, City Civil Court, Chennai.

entities.text: Principal District Judge, City Civil Court, Chennai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 8. The learned Government Advocate has submitted that there are 13 OPs pending before the Court by similarly affected persons and 287 claimants are available in the said OPS who are contesting the same and it will be difficult for the court to transfer all those records to this Court and there may be some kind of orders being passed which is contrary to the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis order that will be passed by the said court in Dharmapuri.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the revision petition.

9. Taking into consideration the facts and the submissions made by both counsel, this Court is of the view that the matter need not be transferred from Principal District Court, Dharmapuri to Chennai instead of the petitioner can be represented by the competent Advocate who will be in a position to follow the matter and as and when it is necessary for examination of the witnesses, the petitioner who is aged about 88 years can be examined by an Advocate Commissioner who would make necessary arrangements for taking his evidence or deposition.

The petitioner is hereby permitted to take out appropriate application at the relevant point of time and the trial Court is directed to consider the same and pass appropriate orders by appointing an Advocate Commissioner in case if it is not possible, the same can be done by way of a Video Conferencing by the Court which ever is comfortable and feasible at this juncture.
The mode of examination conducted can be decided at that point of time.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 10.
With the above directions, the Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition is disposed of.
No order as to costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
